Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of the Iron Pennsylvania Land Reed Huffman DFM-10 Coalbed Methane Well on 10/17/2022. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/29/2025 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Wyalusing Township, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/29/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8215305
Permit API: 015-23923
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/29/2025
Comments: On 01/29/2025 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's (Expand's) STETHERS Location Well Pad in Wyalusing Township, Bradford County. The weather was 43 degrees and cloudy. I arrived at 0945 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed.There were four sand silos onsite. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. There was an above grove storage tank with a liner onsite. Three industrial containment solutions tanks were labeled residual waste and were observed not on containment (photo #6). A representative informed the DEP that they are not in use at this time. There was a dumpster labeled residual waste with improper lining and no secondary containment observed (photo #9). Pooled water off of the pad wide containment was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~ 19.99 mS/cm (photo #11-13). The DEP collected samples (photo #13). There was a representative onsite at the time of the inspection. The DEP informed the representative of the elevated pooled water onsite and that samples were collected. The representative stated he would inform Steve Moyer and they would begin the clean up process. The DEP contacted Steve Moyer via phone call and left a message. The DEP spoke with representative Mike Deming at 1400 hours. He stated he was onsite. He stated equipment surrounding the area of elevated conductivity will be removed and the pooled water will be recovered to begin the clean up process. The DEP recommends:1. Properly recovering and disposing of water held within the truck loading/off loading secondary containment and the pad wide secondary containment (photo #10). 2. Addressing the improper lining of the residual waste dumpster and putting it on secondary containment (photo #9). 3. When the three industrial containment solution tanks are being used they be put on secondary containment. 4. Properly recovering and disposing of the pooled water off of the containment one the south side of the pad (photo #11-13). Based on the elevated electrical conductivity fluids discovered outside of secondary containment a violation of CLS 402(b) (35 P.S. 691.402(b)) is sited against API #015-23923 at this time. Additional violations may be cited against API #015-23923 pending sample results. I departed at 1020 hours.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 992311
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 2.60 mS/cm. Multiple seeps were observed coming from the well pad side slope and the topsoil stockpile which were flowing into the sump. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

Inspection Date: 10/07/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Repsol's Bowers 408 well site located in Jackson Township, Tioga County on 10/7/2024 at 1340 hours. The weather was 60 degrees F with mostly cloudy skies. An Act 9 sign remains in place at the site entrance. The Bowers 408 1H well is capable of producing onsite. Areas surrounding the well pad remain permanently stabilized with vegetative cover. No evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. New material has been added to the access road and regraded since the last DEP inspection. Secondary containment liners remain intact and show no evidence of leaking at this time. A puddle on the pad surface that was field measured for electrical conductivity returned a reading of ~310us/cm. Fluid filled the Bowers 408 1H well cellar and was field measured for electrical conductivity at ~7.15mS/cm today. Due to the elevated electrical conductivity (EC) fluid present, I collected a sample for standard analysis code (SAC) 942 from the well cellar (sample #0983-462). The sample is shown in photos #6 and 7 next to the sample location of the well cellar. A concrete pad surrounds the well cellar (photo #8) and was dry today. Soils located on the edge of the concrete pad were field measured for EC and returned readings below 1.0mS/cm. No distressed vegetation was observed near the concrete pad or anywhere else onsite. All other fluids observed outside of secondary containment were field measured below 1.0mS/cm today.I contacted a representative with Repsol to report my findings and they indicated that they would look into it. On 10/8/2024, Repsol contacted me to indicate that the fluids held within the well cellar were recovered. Repsol explained that the cellar wall was constructed of corrugated metal and has deteriorated over time. Repsol would continue to monitor the wellhead and equipment onsite to try to determine why the fluid in the well cellar had elevated EC. The DEP recommends further evaluation to determine if any of the fluid was able to escape the cellar or infiltrate into the ground.Due to the findings of this inspection report and the elevated EC fluids discovered outside of secondary containment, a violations of CSL 402(b) is cited against API #117-20325 at this time. Additional violations may be cited based on the analytical results from sample #0983-462. I departed the site at 1540 hours.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple releases on Pad B for which violations remain outstanding. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. Some fluid was seeping into this trench from the fill material surrounding the well cellar for well B-11H. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was 2.45 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. The north central area of the well pad has been excavated. One area is a long horizontal area approximately two feet of the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid here was 3.35 to 5.41 mS/cm. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B on permit 081-21880.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid from the MASS from 12/19/22.

Comments: On February 27, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection on the Hillview Cemetery 2 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. No response of any kind to IR 3872789 has been received from the operator as of the date of this inspection. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 5). The brine tank is disconnected from the well equipment at the time of inspection (see photo 6). No evidence of leaks or distressed vegetation was observed where the disconnected line is located. The brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no staining or distressed vegetation on the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). The API number and a means to identify and/or contact the operator have not been posted onsite since the time of IR 3872789. What appears to be sedimentation was observed immediately downslope of the area of most severe rutting in access road (see photo 9). It does not appear to have reached the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued under IR 3872789 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since IR 3872789 was conducted.The Department recommends that the brine tank is removed from site if it is no longer in use for production, in accordance with OGA3216(C).

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TURM OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2022
Violation Code: CSL 307(a) - INDUSTRIAL WASTE DISCHARGES - Industrial waste discharged, directly or indirectly, into Waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit, authorization, or contrary to rules and regulations of the Department.
Violation ID: 957713
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Approximately 5 gallons of produced water.EQT, Moody and SPSI was on site during spill remediation. EQT stated to the department onsite that this spill will be going ACT 2 due to additional observations.The following was observed during inspection:- The Act 9 sign was located at the access road entrance in accordance with 78a55 requirements. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) was on site in mailbox (Photo 1)-Well site entrance and access road appear to be maintained (Photo 2).-I observed fluid actively flowing within well pad drainage. EQT stated to the department that the valves were shut off once spill was found (Photo 4 and 5).-Roll off dumpster was observed onsite for spill remediation. Additional roll of dumpster was delivered during inspection (Photo 7,8,19).-13H GPU check valve resulted in the spill. SPSI was actively remediating and removing impacted material during inspection. Spill occurred between 5H and 13H GPU. Impacted material and elevated readings were found along 5H and 13H GPU. I observed GPU wasn't within secondary containment (Photo 9-15).-Equipment access road was underneath and along 21H GPU and additional GPUs (Photo 16-18).-Well head and well sign was observed (Photo 20).-It appears the spill reached the well pad drainage outlets. I observed elevated conductivity readings of 3.07 mS/cm, 5.17 mS/cm, 5.82 mS/cm and 6.14 mS/cm - 200 ft from GPU spill location at the drainage outlet and collection channel. It appears Waters of the Commonwealth is impacted (Photo 21-25).Field scout conductivity probe was calibrated on 01/24/25 before inspection was conducted.Violations are being issued for: 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 78a.54, 91.34(a), CSL 301, CSL 307(a).

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Comments: On 07/20/2022, The Department received a call from Brian Haner, stating a tree had fallen on a the well overnight and had broken the gathering lines. There was crude getting into a unnamed tributary of Irvine run. An estimated 2+ barrels made its way off site. Upon arrival on site Mr. Haner had booms across the unnamed tributary in several locations. There was a small under flow dam built on a spring seep just below the well. There were also several booms placed at the mouth of the unnamed tributary to Irvine run. Oil absorbent pads were being used to collect oil behind the booms. The crude made its way from the well pad down to a spring seep approx 10-15 feet. The crude continued down the spring into an unnamed tributary of Irvine run approx 140 feet. The spill then continued down the unnamed tributary approx. 1/4 mile. There is some evidence of crude in Irvine run at this time but it is slight. Rain is predicted over the coming days. We spoke with Mr. Haner about placing some booms in a better suited areas. Rain is predicted and the unnamed tributary is prone rise very quickly with small amounts of precipitation. The unnamed trib channel is boulder strewn and very rocky. He said he would move the booms around and monitor them going forward. Mr. Haner also had a excavator in route. He was going to get the impacted soil nearest the well dug up and into containers. He was also going to better construct the underflow dam that was built in the spring flow area just below the well pad. The under flow that was built was functioning but with any appreciable amount of rain it may not handle the added flow.

Comments: I arrived onsite at 1305 to conduct a routine complete inspection of the Corbin Well Pad.The inspection consisted of checking the mailbox for required documents, inspecting all areas of the site for E and S/stabilization issues, and a cursory inspection of the production equipment for any obvious issues. The site's ESCGP expired in 2022 but PCSM stormwater control measures (SCMs ) were never installed. As a result, the permit is still active and has not been terminated. Violations were noted in the most recent inspection of the site (SAIR #4168712). In a written response to that inspection, the operator stated that they had encountered several roadblocks when attempting to implement the PCSM plan. These include the identification of new wetlands where they had planned to place the proposed SCMs and the landowners request that they do not cut down any more trees within the LOD. These two issues reportedly restricted where the operator could place new SCMs. They stated that, as a result of the restrictions these two issues present, the site will have to be re-permitted. They estimated that the new permit package will be submitted in Fall 2026 with construction to begin shortly thereafter if weather permits. As of the date of inspection, no permit package has been received. Please see photos/findings for additional details regarding observations made during the inspection.Continuing violations noted.

Comments: On 07/02/24 an incident inspection of the Walker 1 Well Site was conducted in response to the report of a spill received by the Department on 07/02/24. (CTS: 381922). Background:On 07/02/24 Greylock self-reported a brine release at the Walker 1 well. On 07/02/24 I spoke to Trevor Woods of Greylock to acquire additional details about the spill. During the inspection it was determined that an estimated 60 barrels of produced water had been released to the well area from a crack at the bottom of the poly tank being used on site. Investigation showed that the release was contained to the well area and no water ways were impacted. Remediation efforts were underway at the time of my inspection. Findings:-A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo #1).-The spill is suspected to have originated from a crack at the bottom of the tank (Photos #2-3).-Elevated conductivity was observed in the substrate in the spill area (Photos #4-9). -Crews were present on-site working to remediate the spill. (Photo #10). -No elevated conductivity was observed outside of the spill area.No discharge to surface water was observed. Violations of 78.57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued for the release of brine to the ground.

Violation ID: 925829
Permit API: 081-21877
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/09/2021
Comments: On August 9, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response to a spill at EQT COP Tract 551 Pad B. The spill of drilling mud outside of containment was reported on August 6, 2021. The DEP staff met with EQT company man R.D. Mann. Mr. Mann showed the DEP where the spill occurred and explained that a mud line ruptured outside containment. The area had already been excavated and the impacted soil had been removed prior to the inspection. Two ditches were dug to remove the impacted soil and the impacted soil was removed and back filled on the traveling lane of the well pad. The ditch 1 dug was about 20 feet by 3 feet and about 3 feet deep. Ditch 2 was about 15 ft by 4 feet and about 2 feet deep. The estimation of the amount of oil based mud was about 4.2 barrels spilled, not 42 gallons as the detail sheet states. The spill occurred near the sump and french drain that had been dug for a prior release. The DEP recommended vacuuming the water out of Ditch 1 prior to back filling. Another area of the well pad had been scraped to allow water that is leeching from under the secondary containment of the drilling rig to pool and be vacuumed. The water that is leaching from under the containment is from a previously discovered brine spill. The conductivity of the water in the pool was 848 uS/cm. The DEP recommends monitoring the conductivity of the water that becomes pooled. Precision Drilling 110 is onsite and in the process of drilling the fourth well out of nine wells planned for the well pad. Secondary containment berms and liner where it could be observed was in good condition. There were 4 cement silos and 14 baker tanks onsite in secondary containment. The release of drilling mud outside of containment is violation of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. Violations remain outstanding from Inspection Report 3207564.

Comments: On Wednesday, 12/14/2022, I conducted a routine inspection of the Diversified Production, LLC McIntyre 1 well, permit number 005-29235. The well is located in the woods off of Coal Bank Road in Gilpin township, Armstrong county. The well is in production and had a reported production of 5,341.89 mcf for 2021. There is a well id tag attached to the well head and a well site id sign is posted on the production chart box. The site is restored, but the operator has not maintained the E and S BMP's for the site and there is an area of standing/ponded water on the access road near the site entrance (see picture #8) that needs to be addressed. The site cannot be considered stabilized due to this area and also the area of dead vegetation that was caused by brine being sprayed from a broken pipe onto the brine tank and ground. The brine tank itself is stable and appears to be structurally sound, but the pipe into the brine tank from the gas separator has rusted through and broken off, spraying brine onto the outside of the tank and onto the ground (see pictures #6 and #7). The amount of brine released appears to be less than 1 bbl. These conditions have resulted in violations to 25 PA Code 78.57(a), 25 PA Code 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1) and CSL 402(b) being cited. Although there were no violations cited, the deficiencies on the access road need to be addressed while the operator is addressing the conditions that resulted in the cited violations.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2026 to EQT ARO LLC in Cascade Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8276364
Permit API: 081-20961
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/02/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 6/1/26 a release of an unknown volume of brine-contaminated stormwater occurred outside of containment. The notification also stated that Tobias was dispatched on the morning of 6/2/26 to conduct excavation of impacted pad material. A wireline operator was working on the 5H well when I arrived on location. An aboveground storage tank (AST) is present on the pad along with a gas buster tank. Well site secondary containment consisting of a secondary containment liner, containment berms, and rig mats is present around the well heads. Fluid was present on the containment. Fluid was observed on the pad surface on the north side and on the south side of the containment. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid on the north side of the containment ranged from 1 mS/cm to 2.27 mS/cm. On the south side of the containment the soil is damp but no ponded fluid was observed. The soil EC probe gave a reading of 1.07 mS/cm where the soil was the most damp. On the containment, the EC of the fluid ranged from 700 uS/cm to 3.25 mS/cm. The rest of the well pad and surrounding area appeared very dry.During this inspection, crews were working to remove the fluid from the containment, remove rig mats from the containment, and identify holes in the containment liner. Tobias was also onsite with excavation equipment and a roll-off box. Before I left the location, Tobias began to excavate the impacted pad material and place it into the roll-off box.I met with EQT representative Zac Subra during this inspection. He said that the well site secondary containment had been installed on 5/11/26 for upcoming refrac operations on the 5H well. He also said that the AST was for freshwater to be used for hydrostatic testing of the well. He said that a workover rig has prepped the 5H well for the upcoming refrac and there had been tanks containing produced fluid on the pad at that time. He said that some volume of produced fluid must have been released to the containment. He relayed that crews had so far found 3 holes in the secondary containment liner. He said that the gas buster tank on the pad was empty.I took sample 0718-273 from the pad surface north of the well site secondary containment. I took sample 0718-274 from the fluid on the well site secondary containment.On the same day at 1203, I spoke with Rick Hall of EQT. He stated that on the morning of 6/1/26, the fluid on the pad surface was initially observed and the EC was 1 mS/cm. He said the fluid was checked again throughout the day and the EC climbed until it reached 3.2 mS/cm by the evening. He said they took a sample of the fluid at that time. He said the notification to the Department was made the following morning. I recommended to him that EQT pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown release volume and he said they would. Violations noted.

Comments: On March 10 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the CFR/USX 5 OG Well in regards to OGI referral.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department traveled down the access road towards the well site. Approximately halfway down the access road, the Department observed water flowing onto the access road. The water was observed continuing to flow down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water.Upon further inspection, the water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet. Based on these observations, it appears the water is flowing from the drainage channel/trib to Antram Run onto the access road rather than through the culvert.Upon further inspection of the well site, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head, however had a previous operator listed (Apex Energy). No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead.A well posting was observed on a piece of production equipment and appeared to have all required information. However, it appeared damage and almost falling off. A production tank was observed onsite and appeared in sound condition. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface around the production tank.Prior to leaving the site the Department spoke with operator representative Heather Empfield and informed her of the E and S issues related to the access road caused by the flowing water as well as recommended a new well tag/well posting be installed at the well site.Ms. Empfield stated that she would contact the site foreman to inform them of the Department's observations and they would work to assess the site and correct any issues as necessary.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed erosion of the access road, failure to maintain the culvert, as well as failure to have the well properly posted.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/14/2025
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8234369
Permit API: 125-27157
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Independence Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/14/2025
Comments: On May 14, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Fred Jones well site in Independence Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination request was approved for this site on January 5, 2017. Dylan Stanley, Expand Energy Lease Operator, was onsite during this inspection. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the eastern cutslope of the well pad, which was reported to the DEP by the Expand Energy representative Jared Shockey on May 7, 2025. The DEP spoke Mr. Shockey on May 12, 2025, who stated that Expand Energy recently acquired this site and discovered the reported slough on the eastern cutslope upon assessing the site after acquisition. The slough is reportedly 1.5 feet deep and 100 feet long by 40 feet wide. The operator proposes to remove the sloughed material and add R4 riprap in its place as permanent stabilization.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). However, it appears to be heavily deteriorated with cracks forming in its reflective layer. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan are onsite. However, they are severely waterlogged and could not be evaluated during this inspection (see photo 2). GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a (see photo 16). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 17). Some rainwater was observed in the secondary containment of the production tanks (see photo 18). Well 206H appears to be equipped for production with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it observed (see photo 19). The faded well tag is completely illegible (see photo 20). There are two additional well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photos 21-24). The DEP spoke with Mr. Stanley onsite who stated that an order has already been placed for replacement well tags. The DEP recommended that the secondary containment of the production tanks is kept empty so it can function property in the event of a release. The DEP also recommended replacing the Act 9 sign and ERP onsite to ensure continued compliance post acquisition of site.The access road appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed (see photo 3). The slough that was reported by the operator on 5/07/2025 is present on the eastern cutslope of well pad. Its size appears to fit the dimensions reported by the operator. It does not appear to pose a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth at the time of inspection. A toe bulge was observed below the slough and possible additional cracking was observed at the southern end of the slough (see photos 5-15).Based on observations from this inspection, the DEP recommends that the operator install a new Act 9 sign, well tags, ERP, and PPC plan that are updated with the information of the current operator and comply with current regulations. The DEP also recommends that the operator monitor the slough on the eastern cutslope of the well pad for any additional soil movement and implement temporary stabilization on exposed soil.Violations shall be issued against the slough on the eastern cutslope of the well pad.The following information is requested from the operator:- What is being done in the interim (temporary stabilization)- What is being done in the future (permanent stabilization)If a Geotechnical Report would be necessary and/or developed for the soil crack and/or slough, please submit to DEP Technical Services. The Department recommends that the Operator coordinate with DEP Technical Services for any potential modifications to the approved ESCGP plans that may be necessary for addressing the soil crack and/or slough.

A 24 hour pressure build up test was conducted concluding on 8/12/2021 at 10:00 AM. 28% gas was detected at the source of the bubbling. 0 PSI was observed on the 20" x 13 3/8" annulus vent with no gas to sample. 53 PSI and 44% gas was detected on the 13 3/8" x 9 5/8" annulus vent. 71 PSI and 75% gas was detected on the 9 5/8" x 5 1/2" annulus vent. Creston took sample where gas was detected. A 0 to 5k PSI analog pressure gauge was attached to the well head reading approximately 0 PSI. Well is scheduled to be completed in early September.
